title: FSD P8 issues no requirement ID, so the product requirement cannot be traced to an FSD requirement
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5)
section: Requirements served; T8 Requirement traceability
description: The FSD P8 v3 table 'Requirements served' has its header row and no data row, and the TSD P8 v2 section T8 'Requirement traceability' has its header row and no data row. Every other module FSD names the REQ IDs it serves, so a PRD for this service has no FSD requirement ID to map to. The functional substance exists in the feature set (FEAT-PAY-01 to FEAT-PAY-11) and in the acceptance criteria (AC-P8-xxx, AC-ALT-P8-xxx, AC-EXC-P8-xxx).
evidence: FSD P8 v3 lines under 'Requirements served' (header only); TSD P8 v2 T8 (header only); the program BRD states that P8 has no requirement section of its own (section 11 note; CG-B-REQ-BRD-PROG-8).
proposed: Trace every product requirement to the FSD feature ID and the FSD acceptance criterion ID, and cite the BRD requirement it serves. Ask the FSD owner to fill the two tables in the next FSD version, or to state that P8 has no requirement ID of its own.

title: Eight of the eleven P8 features carry a placeholder acceptance criterion instead of a testable one
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
section: A2.3.4.1 to A2.11.4.1 (main success flow)
description: AC-P8-003-01 to AC-P8-011-01 read 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version', with the story cell 'Written one epic ahead'. Only FEAT-PAY-01 and FEAT-PAY-02 (A2.1 and A2.2) carry a worked example with a payment, a case and a business date. Settlement matching, auction and enforcement proceeds, fees, booking, ledger posting, provision inputs, the deed in lieu auto-debit, the application of proceeds and the daily reconciliation therefore have no testable main-flow criterion in the source.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.3.4.1, A2.4.4.1, A2.5.4.1, A2.6.4.1, A2.7.4.1, A2.8.4.1, A2.9.4.1, A2.10.4.1, A2.11.4.1 (identical placeholder rows); the exception rows of the same features are substantive.
proposed: This PRD writes the criteria for those features from the feature statement, the business rules and the field list, and marks them as new. The FSD owner confirms or replaces them before wave 3 system test.

title: The two operations named in Architecture v5 slide 17 are not the two operations in the API Specification and the Ownership Map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Slide 17 rwb-payment IN; API Specification /proceeds and /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match; Ownership Map api sheet
description: Architecture v5 slide 17 gives the rwb-payment contract as 'REST GET /cases/{id}/payments' and 'POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate (manual)'. The API Specification v4 and the Ownership Map name GET /proceeds and POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match, both with x-module P8, first release E2 and E4. The two pairs describe the same two capabilities - the receipt list and the manual match - with different paths, different resource names and different verbs (allocate against match).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 17 ('REST GET /cases/{id}/payments - POST /proceeds/{id}/allocate (manual)'); slide 41 service catalogue row for P8 gives '/cases/{id}/payments'; API Specification v4 lines for /proceeds (operationId getProceeds) and /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match (operationId postProceedsProceedsidMatch); Ownership Map: both operations owner P8.
proposed: Publish one pair of operations in the wave-2 contract. This PRD takes the API Specification pair as the contract, because it is the artifact with a schema and an operation identifier, and reads the slide 17 names as the same two capabilities under older naming. Confirm before the contract story is closed.

title: The data quality exception list that holds an unmatched payment has no home in v5
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: AC-EXC-P8-001-02 places payment 'PAY-90003', whose account is on no open case, on 'the data quality exception list with check References'. The FSD P1 v3 change note records that the Workbench holds no inbound load, load run or data quality exception after D-RCV-35, and the Ownership Map has no quality-exception table; the reconciliation result and the break list of rwb-source-data are the only quality surfaces in v5. The AC therefore names a table that does not exist.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 AC-EXC-P8-001-02 and AC-EXC-P8-002-02; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 change note (no inbound load, load run or data quality exception); Ownership Map tables sheet (no quality exception table; P1 owns reconciliation_result).
proposed: Report the orphan as a break row on the reconciliation break list of rwb-source-data with the check name 'References', and write no exception table in rwb_payment. Confirm the check name with the data steward.

title: The matching values have no table and no owner after payment_match_rule was retired
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5) T3.1; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: T3.1 payment_match_rule (DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273); rule-package section
description: The TSD defines payment_match_rule in this module with the amount tolerance, the window days before and after, the grace days, the partial floor and the priority. The data dictionary records every one of those fields as 'Retired by D-RCV-36', and the Ownership Map has no payment_match_rule row. The Temporal and Drools design makes PAYMENT_MATCH one of the three named Phase 1 rule packages, governed in rwb-decision and evaluated in the owning service, while the R-PREC default ruling sends parameters (E1-042) and reference data (E1-043) to rwb-case. Where the values live is therefore open; only the product duty (values in force, version recorded) is fixed.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (payment_match_rule, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273); LDM and Data Dictionary v8 rows DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 ('Retired by D-RCV-36'); Temporal and Drools design (PAYMENT_MATCH, BOOKING_MATCH, RESTRUCTURE are the named Phase 1 packages); Ownership Map parameter_catalog, parameter_value, reference_row, rule_package owner rows.
proposed: Hold the values as versioned parameter or reference rows read through the rwb-case contract, and the match logic as the PAYMENT_MATCH package fetched from rwb-decision. Confirm which of the two carries the tolerance and window values before the first match runs.

title: Settlement booking confirmation is Epic 3 work in the BRD and Epic 4 work in the FSD
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (03 Requirements and specifications); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epic 2 v3
section: FSD A2.6 (first in E4); Epics 3 to 8 BRD 7.3 and dependency table (E3 booking)
description: FEAT-PAY-06 'Post a settlement booking to ALS' has its first release in E4 in the FSD feature overview. The Epics 3 to 8 BRD names rwb-payment as an Epic 3 service, and its dependency table writes 'Payment and proceeds matching, fees and posting | rwb-payment | E3 booking, E4 proceeds, E6 write-off'. E3 releases on 31 January 2027 and E4 on 28 February 2027, and the business epic wave map gives EP03 wave 2 and EP04 wave 3.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A1.2 feature overview row FEAT-PAY-06 (First in E4); Epics 3 to 8 BRD 7.3 (E3 and E4 name RWB-SVC-P8) and dependency row DEP-005; Program BRD 8 (release plan) and 10.3 (waves).
proposed: Build the booking confirmation in wave 2 with EP03, the earlier of the two dates, because a settlement that is booked in E3 must be confirmed in the same release; the proceeds features stay in wave 3.

title: The posting file has no layout, no schedule and no receiving ledger in any source
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17
section: FSD A2.7; TSD T5.1 (INT-16); Arch v5 slide 17 OUT (deliverFile, posting file)
description: FEAT-PAY-07 posts accounting entries for settlements, sales and write-offs to the ledger, and Arch v5 gives rwb-payment the output 'Integration: deliverFile (posting file)'. No source states the file layout, the entry types, the value date rule, the run schedule, the ledger that receives it or what the ledger returns. The TSD interface INT-16 says only 'GL | In | File load | Monthly', which contradicts a posting that follows each booked settlement.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.7 (integration points 'ALS and GL'); TSD P8 v2 T5.1 row INT-16; Arch v5 slide 17 OUT line; Ownership Map api and tables sheets have no posting-file table for P8.
proposed: Fix one line per posting with case, account key, entry type, amount, value date, business date and posting reference, a manifest with count and checksum, and delivery through rwb-integration. Agree the layout with Finance and the ledger owner before wave 3.

title: The FSD names ALS, GL, ATS and AMIS as interface points, and v5 lets no service call a system of record
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 41
section: FSD A2.1.2 to A2.11.2 (integration points); TSD T5.1 (INT-02, INT-03, INT-16)
description: The FSD gives 'ALS and GL' as the integration points of nine features, 'ALS and GL, LED portal' for enforcement proceeds and 'ATS, AMIS' for the deed in lieu rental. Under D-RCV-35 and ADR-010 the Workbench reads source data only through the rwb-source-data views, writes no booking into ALS (the officer books it), and no v5 catalogue lists an ATS, AMIS or LED interface. The product duty survives; the route does not exist yet.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 integration points of A2.1, A2.3 to A2.11; TSD P8 v2 T5.1 (INT-02 COLLINS batch in, INT-03 booked by the officer, INT-16 GL file in); Arch v5 slide 13 and slide 41 (no direct call to a system of record; INT-19 and INT-20 removed); Program BRD REQ-DRI-006.
proposed: Read the ALS position through the rwb-source-data contract after the next completed ACE batch, deliver ledger postings out through rwb-integration, and treat the auto-debit and LED routes as outside the 19 services until an interface is named.

title: A reversed payment has no product behaviour in the FSD although the routing rules require the case to reopen
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
section: Routing logic R-SET-23, R-SET-24; Temporal design settlement notes
description: The routing logic requires a payment reversal after release to reopen the case (R-SET-23, R-SET-24) and the Temporal design repeats it as a settlement risk. The FSD P8 has no feature, no rule and no acceptance criterion for a reversal: there is no reversal source value, no state on the proceeds record and no event. The unmatched and matched flows assume a receipt that stays valid.
evidence: Routing Logic v4 R-SET-23 ('PAYMENT_REVERSED | reversal received after release') and R-SET-24; Temporal and Drools design ('payment reversed -> case reopens', 'S2 settlement: payment reversal reopens the case (R-SET-23/24)'); FSD P8 v3 A1.2 feature list (no reversal feature).
proposed: Decide whether a reversal is in scope for this service. If it is, add a reversal source value, a reversal state on the proceeds record and an event that reopens the case through rwb-case. Until then the capability is out of scope and listed as an open question.

title: The fee tables that the fee feature reads are not defined anywhere
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (03 Requirements and specifications)
section: FSD A2.5; TSD T3.1 (no fee table); Ownership Map tables sheet
description: FEAT-PAY-05 works out partner fees, court fees and charges 'from the fee tables held as data', and FEAT-WOF-15 and FEAT-PRM-06 depend on the same schedule. The TSD field list defines only proceeds and payment_match_rule; the Ownership Map has no fee table, no fee schedule and no list of values for a fee type; the Epics 3 to 8 BRD names the fee requirement and no rate, basis, cap or table.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.5.2 (integration points 'Workbench, ALS and GL'); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.2 (no fee object, no fee list); Ownership Map tables sheet (no fee table); Epics 3 to 8 BRD BR-033 and REQ-S9-004.
proposed: Name the fee table, its owner and its schedule, and hold the fee rate, the cap and the basis as versioned rows. Until then the fee calculation has no input and the feature cannot be tested.

title: The proceeds record names the ACE payment twice, once as a uuid cross-reference and once as a business key
source: Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 (03 Requirements and specifications)
section: TSD T3.1 DF-FIN-004 account_payment_id; API schema Proceeds.paymentCode; Program BRD REQ-CHO-009 and 5.3
description: The TSD defines account_payment_id as a CROSS_REF of type uuid with cardinality 'many to 0 or 1' to account_payment, which reads as a link into another schema. The API Specification declares paymentCode as varchar(255) with the description 'ACE payment_code of the payment matched (v_ace_payment); business key, no foreign key'. The program requirement matches by the ACE payment_code, and v5 forbids a foreign key into ACE and a cross-schema reference.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (DF-FIN-004 account_payment_id, CROSS_REF, uuid) and T3.3 (proceeds to account_payment, many to 0 or 1); API Specification v4 Proceeds.paymentCode; Program BRD REQ-CHO-009 ('matched ... by the ACE payment_code'); ADR-014 and DP-01.
proposed: Keep one business-key column of type varchar(255) holding the ACE payment_code with no foreign key, as the API Specification and the program requirement both say, and drop the uuid cross-reference from the field list.

title: The daily money reconciliation compares to a ledger position the Workbench does not receive
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench TSD P8 Payments and posting v2 (_work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17
section: FSD A2.11; TSD T5.1 INT-16
description: FEAT-PAY-11 compares what the Workbench matched to what ALS and the ledger show, every day. The ALS position can be read through v_ace_payment and v_ace_account after the completed batch; the ledger position has no feed: INT-16 is a monthly inbound file load, which is removed in v5, and rwb-payment sends a posting file out without receiving a return. A daily comparison to the ledger therefore has one side missing.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.11.2 (integration points 'ALS and GL'); TSD P8 v2 T5.1 row INT-16 ('GL | In | File load | Monthly'); Arch v5 slide 17 OUT (deliverFile with the posting file only).
proposed: Reconcile to the ACE payment and account position and to the posting file this service delivered and rwb-integration confirms. Add a ledger return only if the ledger owner publishes one, and record the choice as an open question until then.

title: The order in which a receipt is applied to the balance is named but not specified
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (03 Requirements and specifications)
section: FSD A2.10 ('in the order the policy sets'); Epics 3 to 8 BRD BR-030
description: FEAT-PAY-10 applies every receipt 'in the order the policy sets', and BR-030 says only that sale proceeds are applied and a shortfall raised. No source states the order (principal, interest, fees, costs, or another sequence), who owns it, or where it is held. The requirement that it must be data is fixed by principle 1; the sequence itself is not.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.10.2; FSD BR-P8-010 ('No value a business person may change is written in code'); Epics 3 to 8 BRD BR-030; no order row in the Ownership Map or the parameter catalog extract.
proposed: Hold the application order as versioned rows with an owner and a valid-from date, record the version on each proceeds row, and let Finance set the sequence before wave 3.

title: The two run messages of this module have no wording in the message standard
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
description: The exception flows use MSG-P8-001 in the run summary ('1 unmatched payment for 2026-12-14') and MSG-P8-002 for a run with no matching values in force. Neither is in the Error and Message Standard extract, and neither states its Thai wording, its channel (screen, run summary or both) or whether it blocks. MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-002 are used with their source wording.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 AC-EXC-P8-001-01 and AC-EXC-P8-001-05; the message IDs appear nowhere else in the extract set.
proposed: Keep the two message IDs and their intent, and take the wording and the Thai text from the message standard when it is published. Confirm whether MSG-P8-001 is a screen message, a run summary line or both.

title: The only success measure of the module has no baseline and no measurement definition
source: Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
section: A2.1.1 to A2.11.1 (metric table, identical in every feature)
description: Every P8 feature repeats the metric 'Receipts matched the same day | Rising each month | Decision log and Workbench records | Monthly'. There is no baseline, no percentage target, no definition of 'the same day' (the receipt date, the business date or the calendar day of the run) and no stated population. The measure cannot be tested or reported as written.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.1.1 to A2.11.1 metric tables; Program BRD 2 (business outcomes) sets no receipt-matching measure.
proposed: Take the measure from the decision log as the FSD says, and have the product owner set the baseline, the target and the definition of 'the same day' before the wave-2 release note.

title: The two event-started workflows have no name or identifier in any v5 source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Slide 44 job map (JOB-07, JOB-08); Ownership Map jobs and workflows sheets
description: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-07 and JOB-08 as event-triggered workflows in rwb-payment and the Ownership Map records the replacement as 'event-started workflow (matchPayments in rwb-payment)' and 'confirmBookings'. The workflows sheet of the Ownership Map lists fifteen workflows and none belongs to P8, and the Temporal design names the activities, not the workflows. A schedule or a workflow that has no name cannot be referenced by a story or a test.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 rows JOB-07 and JOB-08; Ownership Map jobs sheet (replacement text) and workflows sheet (no P8 row); Temporal design ('Act: matchPayments, confirmBookings', 'Act: postProceeds (saga step)').
proposed: Name the two event-started workflows after their activity (matchPayments, confirmBookings) and register them on the task queue rwb-payment, or confirm that the activity alone is the unit.

title: Payment received is a named same-day trigger under DL06 and the matching run is once per business date
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 (03 Requirements and specifications) section 9 (DL06); Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
section: Program BRD DL06; FSD A2.1.4.4 (system background events); Arch v5 slide 44
description: DL06 names 'case transferred from EFS, payment received, legal event' as the same-day triggers, and states that ACE has no real-time feed today. The FSD starts the matching run on the completed ACE batch for ALS, once a day, and Architecture v5 gives JOB-07 as an event-started workflow on AceDataReady. A payment received after the batch is therefore matched on the next business date, which contradicts the same-day intent of DL06 for this service.
evidence: Program BRD v5 DL06 ('Name the same-day triggers now: case transferred from EFS, payment received, legal event'; 'ACE has no real time feed today'); FSD P8 v3 AC-BG-P8-001-01 ('ACE batch for source ALS complete, Daily'); Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-07 on the ACE batch-complete record).
proposed: Keep one run per business date in wave 2 and record the same-day trigger as an open question; add an intraday run only when an interface that carries a payment during the day is named.

title: The program BRD note on P8 requirements leaves out the enforcement proceeds requirement it also cites
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 (03 Requirements and specifications); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (03 Requirements and specifications)
section: Program BRD section 11 note; section 5.11; Epics 3 to 8 BRD BR-043
description: The note after the program requirement trace says P8's requirements 'are carried inside other sections: payment matching and posting in 5.3 and 5.12 to 5.14'. FEAT-PAY-04 (match auction and enforcement proceeds) rests on REQ-S4-010, which sits in section 5.11, and the Epics 3 to 8 BRD states the same requirement in BR-043 with FEAT-LIT-22. A reader who follows the note only would miss the requirement this service serves for enforcement proceeds.
evidence: Program BRD v5 section 11 note; section 5.11 (REQ-S4-010); Epics 3 to 8 BRD BR-043 ('REQ-S4-010; FEAT-LIT-22; RWB-E5-022'); FSD P8 v3 A2.4 and FEAT-PAY-04.
proposed: Read the note as illustrative and cite REQ-S4-010 here as a requirement this service serves, and ask the program BRD owner to add section 5.11 to the note in the next version.

title: No approval is recorded for this product baseline
source: Program BRD v5 section 12; Epic 2 v3 section 10.2; FSD P8 v3 document sign-off
section: Approval and sign-off
description: The program BRD states that it stays in Draft until the Product Owner and the business owner approve it, and records no approval. The FSD P8 sign-off table is empty and names four roles with no signature. This PRD inherits an unapproved baseline and records no approval of its own: the run overlay forbids a human approval stop and the approval table is left empty.
evidence: Program BRD v5 section 12 closing paragraph; Epic 2 v3 section 10.2; FSD P8 v3 'Document sign-off' (empty).
proposed: Keep the status at Draft and the approval table empty, and record the missing approval as an assumption; the Product Owner and the FDA approve the baseline and this PRD together.

title: No receipt volume is stated for the volume test of this service
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 (03 Requirements and specifications); Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3; Recovery Workbench FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6)
section: Program BRD 6.1; NFR Spec v3 section 1 (NFR-001); FSD metric tables
description: NFR-001 states the case volume (about 23,600 open cases at go-live, 3,110 new accounts at 90 days past due a month) and NFR-007 the decision-log size. No source states how many receipts a business date carries, so the volume test of the matching run, the receipt list and the posting run has no stated population.
evidence: NFR Spec v3 NFR-001 and NFR-007; Program BRD 6.1; FSD P8 v3 metric tables (no volume).
proposed: Size the test from the receipt-to-installment ratio observed on the ACE data for a busy month and state the number in the next NFR version; until then the volume test uses the ratio as an assumption.
